newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya's ruling party takes initiative on reforms.
newsitem.headline: Kenya's ruling party takes initiative on reforms.

text.p: Kenya's ruling party has taken the offensive in the country's political crisis, accepting an opposition challenge to make radical changes to controversial laws before national elections this year.

Opposition leaders were digesting Thursday's surprise announcement, but said they would press on with a campaign of mass protests in which at least nine people were killed on July 7 when security forces violently suppressed a rally.

If enacted, the ruling party's recommendations would weaken the power of President Daniel arap Moi, 73, who has ruled since 1978 and faces intense political pressure from an opposition-backed group demanding constitutional reform.
The ruling Kenya African National Union (KANU) also said parliament should set up a body to review the constitution.

KANU Vice-President George Saitoti, who holds the same post in the government, said the law changes and the constitutional review should be carried out before this year's presidential and parliamentary polls.
No date has been set for the polls pitting KANU against an opposition that has found a fragile cohesion in its demands for reform.

"The NEC (KANU National Executive Council) recommends that the government should consider and publish a Bill for enactment by the current parliament providing for the establishment of a Commission to review the constitution of Kenya and make proposals," NEC said in a statement.

"The NEC further recommended that the Government should consider and publish a Statute Law...Bill for enactment by the current parliament which provides for the following laws to be repealed or amended where deemed necessary," it added.
The 11 laws include the Public Order Act used to regulate public gatherings, but vilified as repressive by reformists.

"We will continue the pressure...but the moment we are convinced the government is ready for serious dialogue -- principled dialogue -- we will immediately suspend the mass action," Kivutha Kibwana, a member of the pro-reform National Council Executive Committee (NCEC) told the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Richard Leakey, secretary-general of the unregistered Safina party, said: "If this is actually truthful and it is implemented I think a very great many people in the opposition will be very pleased."
The NCEC on Thursday called for a rally in Kenya's second city Mombasa, centre of its tourism industry on its Indian Ocean coast, on July 26 and a general strike and sit-in on August 8.
